[Skip to content](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/intelligence/ai-integrations#ai-integrations) Copy for LLM [Spacelift Documentation](https://docs.spacelift.io/ "Spacelift Documentation") # AI Integrations [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/intelligence/ai-integrations\#ai-integrations "Anchor link to this section") AI integrations connect [Infra Assistant](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/intelligence/infra-assistant) features to LLM providers. [Intent](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/intelligence/intent) does not use them. When you connect through the [Spacelift MCP server](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/intelligence/spacelift-mcp), your own AI client supplies the model and pays for the tokens. You can either use the Spacelift-provided integration or bring your own. ## Spacelift-provided [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/intelligence/ai-integrations\#spacelift-provided "Anchor link to this section") Every Spacelift account comes with a default AI integration managed by Spacelift. Once [Spacelift Intelligence is enabled](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/intelligence/infra-assistant#enabling-infra-assistant), it needs no configuration. - **Provider**: AWS Bedrock (Anthropic) - **Available models**: Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Opus 4.8 - **API key**: Not required, managed by Spacelift - **Token budget**: Depends on your plan tier. See [Token budget](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/intelligence/infra-assistant#token-budget) for details. This integration appears as _Spacelift default_ in the Infra Assistant model selector. ## Bring Your Own Model (BYOM) [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/intelligence/ai-integrations\#bring-your-own-model-byom "Anchor link to this section") You can configure your own AI provider integrations to use your preferred LLM provider and model with your own API keys. ### Supported providers and models [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/intelligence/ai-integrations\#supported-providers-and-models "Anchor link to this section") Spacelift supports the following providers: **Anthropic**, **Google**, **OpenAI** and **AWS Bedrock**. Models are automatically discovered from the provider's API using the supplied credentials. You can choose which models you want our AI Intelligence to use from the available ones. Well-known non-chat models (e.g. whisper, dall-e) are filtered out and can't be selected. For Anthropic, Google and OpenAI you can also set a custom **base url** to route the integration through a self-hosted, provider-compatible gateway such as [LiteLLM](https://litellm.ai/), or any other service that offers an API compatible with any of the major providers. Note BYOM integrations are billed directly by your provider. Spacelift does not impose any token limits on them. API keys are encrypted at rest. Each integration is scoped to a [Space](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/spaces), which controls which users can access it. You can create multiple integrations for different providers, teams, or environments. ### AWS Bedrock permissions [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/intelligence/ai-integrations\#aws-bedrock-permissions "Anchor link to this section") An AWS Bedrock integration assumes the role on your linked [AWS cloud integration](https://docs.spacelift.io/getting-started/integrate-cloud/AWS) and calls Bedrock from Spacelift's side. That role needs permission to list inference profiles and foundation models, and to invoke models through an inference profile: | | | | --- | --- | | ```

"Effect": "Allow",

"bedrock:InvokeModel",

],
"Resource": [
"arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/*",
"arn:aws:bedrock:*::inference-profile/*"
]
},
{
"Sid": "SpaceliftBedrockList",
"Effect": "Allow",
"Action": [
"bedrock:ListInferenceProfiles",
"bedrock:ListFoundationModels"
],
"Resource": "*"
}
]
}
``` | Replace `` with the account that owns the inference profiles. The invoke actions are granted on both the inference-profile ARNs and the underlying `foundation-model` ARNs on purpose: invoking through a cross-region inference profile requires access to the foundation models in every region the profile routes to, and the region wildcard covers that. The two `List*` actions sit in their own `Resource: "*"` statement because they don't support resource-level scoping in IAM; scoping them to an ARN would leave them ungranted and break profile discovery. Note If setting up the integration succeeds but chats fail with an access-denied error, the usual cause is a missing invoke permission (`bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream`) on the `foundation-model` ARNs. Spacelift can list and validate models with read-only access, but generating a reply needs the invoke action, so the two can fail independently. ## Managing integrations [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/intelligence/ai-integrations\#managing-integrations "Anchor link to this section") Go to **Settings** \> **Integrations** \> **AI** to manage your AI integrations. ![AI integrations list](https://docs.spacelift.io/assets/screenshots/infra-assistant/ai-integrations-list.png) ### Creating an integration [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/intelligence/ai-integrations\#creating-an-integration "Anchor link to this section") 01. Click **Set up integration**. 02. Enter a **Name** for the integration. 03. Optionally add a **Description**. 04. Select a **Space** to scope the integration to. 05. Select a **Provider** (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, or AWS Bedrock). 06. Provide credentials for the selected provider: - **Anthropic / OpenAI / Google**: paste your **API key** from the provider. - **AWS Bedrock**: choose an existing [AWS cloud integration](https://docs.spacelift.io/getting-started/integrate-cloud/AWS) and an AWS region, then pick from the inference profiles Spacelift discovers in that account and region. The AWS integration must **not** have [**Assume role on worker**](https://docs.spacelift.io/getting-started/integrate-cloud/AWS) enabled, because Spacelift assumes its role on its own end to reach Bedrock. Spacelift validates the profiles at save time. 07. Optionally specify a custom **Base URL**. Only `https` URLs are supported. - At save time, Spacelift validates the gateway by checking that the endpoint accepts the API key and issuing a test completion against each selected model. If any model is not reachable, the save fails with an error message listing the failing model(s). 08. Select the **Models** the integration can use. For Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google, Spacelift fetches the available models from the provider API. For AWS Bedrock, the inference profiles chosen in the previous step serve as the model list. 09. Optionally add **Labels** for organization. 10. Click **Set up**. ![AI integration creation form](https://docs.spacelift.io/assets/screenshots/infra-assistant/ai-integration-create.png) Tip You can find API keys from your provider's dashboard: - [Anthropic Console](https://console.anthropic.com/) - [OpenAI Platform](https://platform.openai.com/) - [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/) ### Editing an integration [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/intelligence/ai-integrations\#editing-an-integration "Anchor link to this section") Open an integration from the list to update its name, description, labels, API key, or space assignment. Editing requires the **Update AI integration** permission (or the Space admin role) in the integration's [Space](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/spaces). To change the model selection, re-enter the API key: so Spacelift can fetch the live model list from the provider. The stored key is never displayed. Changing the API key, base URL, or model list re-triggers the save-time validation. Note The Spacelift-provided integration is managed by Spacelift and cannot be edited. You can only enable or disable it (see below). ### Enabling and disabling an integration [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/intelligence/ai-integrations\#enabling-and-disabling-an-integration "Anchor link to this section") You can turn an integration off without deleting it. A disabled integration keeps its configuration but cannot be used: [Infra Assistant](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/intelligence/infra-assistant) rejects any request routed to it until you re-enable it. Toggle an integration from its actions menu in the list, or select several integrations to enable or disable them in bulk. Enabling or disabling an integration requires the **Toggle AI integration** permission (or the Space admin role). For a Space-scoped integration this is checked in the integration's [Space](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/spaces). See [RBAC actions](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/authorization/rbac-system#ai-integration-actions). Because the Spacelift-provided integration has no Space, enabling or disabling it is authorized on your [root space](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/spaces). ### Deleting an integration [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/intelligence/ai-integrations\#deleting-an-integration "Anchor link to this section") Select **Delete** from the actions menu. Conversations that were using the deleted integration will need a new integration selected to continue. ## Selecting an integration in Infra Assistant [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/intelligence/ai-integrations\#selecting-an-integration-in-infra-assistant "Anchor link to this section") In the [Infra Assistant](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/intelligence/infra-assistant) chat, use the model selector to pick which integration and model to use. The dropdown shows _Spacelift default_ (the Spacelift-provided Bedrock integration) along with any BYOM integrations you have access to through your [Space](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/spaces) membership. You can switch integrations at any time during a conversation. When switching between providers, the conversation history is automatically adapted for compatibility with the new model. ![Infra Assistant model selector](https://docs.spacelift.io/assets/screenshots/infra-assistant/chat-model-selector.png) For details on data handling and provider responsibilities, see the [AI Terms of Use](https://docs.spacelift.io/legal/ai-terms).
